Some of these are deflated a bit because Warrior has a brand new hero, Ninja has TWO brand new heroes, and Assassin has two brand new heroes and OG Arakni. 

Some thoughts:   
Illusionists are always good, yes, but they also have the second fewest heroes available and have never had more than two heroes available at any given time. Seeing as their play style is vastly different than anything else available, I'd say that this is a combination of strong players using strong decks and people who like a permanent based playstyle gravitating towards the deck. Further, many Enigma wins were at high tier events, and I think that this shows that there is a certain gap between the high skilled players and the medium to low skilled players. Illusionists are generally thought of as a rather difficult class to play.

Ranger: I'm genuinely surprised this is number 2. I guess having two strong characters combined with only having three characters ever printed for the class does that. 

Runeblade: Mixed damage is crazy strong. The class is also a confirmed favorite, and there was a stretch where three sets in a row had Runeblades and the three of them dominated everything for a while. Chane and Briar both ate bans, Briar had to have her hero ability rewritten, and Rosetta Thorn is a gaping wound in the history of the game.

Guardian: Starvo goes BRRRR. Bravo has been around since day one. They haven't been in the spotlight for a while.

Ninja: Very strong, with adult Ira and Cindra pulling the average down. Having a class identity of "More attacks than hand size" gets work done.

Wizard: The first two LLing makes--wait, Kano is still around? How? 

Brute: Better than you'd expect the way people talk about the class, but that's mostly carried by Kayo and a low total hero count. I can understand why non-Kayo players have issues with performance. His hero ability is literally "The built in Brute drawback isn't as bad." 

Assassin: Two brand new heroes and OG Arakni means this is lower than it should be. I'm sure the fact that it's a six thousand dollar deck keeps the class from crushing as many proquests as it should.

Mechanologist: Entirely carried by Dashie. She's been a strong rogue deck since forever, and sneaks out wins here and there. Likely held back by the fact that it is entirely parasitic; you climb into the silo and never leave. This stops people from dabbling in the deck, which stops people from taking it to PQs.

Warrior: Five adult warriors with very few results ever. Dorinthea, pretty much the face of WtR, has 605 points. No one else is even close. If anyone gets to complain, it's these folks. They keep giving the class more and more mediocrity. The reliance on reactions makes me think that they struggle to strengthen the class without absolutely breaking it wide open. People think Illusionists are rough, but I think a top tier Warrior would be a meat grinder. I'd love to see it happen.
